chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'I was with a judge from the judges of Medina when two men came to him. One of them said: I hired an animal from this man to carry me from such-and-such place to such-and-such place, but it did not deliver me to the destination. The judge asked the owner of the animal: Did you take him to the place? He replied: No, my animal became exhausted and did not reach. The judge said to him: You are not entitled to any fare since you did not deliver him to the place for which you hired your animal.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So I called them both to me and said to the hirer: You are not entitled, O servant of Allah, to take the entire fare of the man's animal. And I said to the other: O servant of Allah, you are not entitled to take the entire fare for your animal, but look at the portion of the journey that remained and the portion that was ridden, and come to an agreement on it.' So they did as instructed.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on payment for hired transport if the journey is not completed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) refutes the judge's rigid 'all-or-nothing' ruling by introducing the principle of proportional compensation (kaffarat al-maslakah), ensuring fairness for both parties in a service contract. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for deriving the rules of *Ijarah* (leasing/renting), emphasizing that partial performance warrants partial payment based on the actual distance covered versus the total agreed distance.
